subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of these is a greenhouse gas?
questions.explain: Methane is a greenhouse gas, along with carbon dioxide and water vapour.

questions.q: Why are fossil fuels described as finite resources?
options: They form much faster than we use them
They are being used up faster than they form
questions.explain: Fossil fuels take millions of years to form, so they are finite and being used up faster than they are replaced.

questions.q: During incomplete combustion of a hydrocarbon, which products may form?
options: Carbon monoxide and/or carbon (soot), and water
questions.explain: Incomplete combustion in limited oxygen can produce carbon monoxide and/or carbon as well as water.

questions.q: What is meant by the carbon footprint of a product?
options: The total greenhouse gases emitted over its life cycle
The amount of carbon it contains only
questions.explain: A carbon footprint is the total amount of greenhouse gases emitted over the full life cycle of a product or service.

questions.q: The early atmosphere is thought to have been mainly which gas, released by volcanoes?
questions.explain: Volcanic activity released large amounts of carbon dioxide into the early atmosphere.

questions.q: Sulfur dioxide released from burning fuels causes which environmental problem?
questions.explain: Sulfur dioxide dissolves in rain water to form acid rain.

questions.q: Poly(ethene) is made from ethene molecules by:
questions.explain: Many ethene (alkene) monomers join in addition polymerisation to form poly(ethene).

questions.q: Crude oil is separated into fractions by fractional distillation according to differences in:
questions.explain: Fractional distillation separates the hydrocarbons by their different boiling points.

questions.q: Why is cracking carried out on some crude oil fractions?
options: Demand for short-chain fractions like petrol is greater than supply
There is too little demand for short-chain hydrocarbons
questions.explain: Cracking matches supply to demand, as there is more demand for short-chain hydrocarbons than the supply from crude oil.

questions.q: Ethanol belongs to which homologous series?
questions.explain: Ethanol is a member of the alcohol homologous series.

questions.q: Incomplete combustion of fuels can produce which toxic gas?
questions.explain: Carbon monoxide is a toxic gas produced by incomplete combustion when oxygen is limited.

questions.q: As the early oceans formed, water vapour in the atmosphere:
questions.explain: As the Earth cooled, water vapour condensed to form the oceans.
